gen-dafont-stentiga-fs-merriweather-sans: Merriweather Sans stands tall and sturdy, a plain sans whose lowercase looks big and whose e opens clearly to the right. Stentiga is the showy one, stencil-cut and spread out, while the body simply gets on with the reading.
gen-dafont-jelly-crazies-fs-be-vietnam-p: Jelly Crazies wobbles along with bowls that nearly seal shut, slowing the eye to a leisurely walk. Be Vietnam Pro sits beside it with sans-serif curves that stay wide open, giving the page somewhere to breathe.
gen-gf-paprika-fs-epilogue: Scattered, spaced-out letters that fill the line like capitals give Paprika its swagger. Epilogue follows in a wire-like monoline with curvy, tall-bodied forms, so the loud heading gets a friendly voice underneath it.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-cascadia-code: Cascadia Code runs on horizontal bars as heavy as its upright stems, a plain sans with generous gaps between neighbors. And Paprika scatters its own letters wide too, so the two share spacing while differing in stroke.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-cascadia-mono: Loud, spread out and unapologetic. Paprika has lowercase that fills the line like capitals, while Cascadia Mono answers with a flat gray hum of constant line weight and letters standing like pins in a board.
gen-gf-snowburst-one-work-sans: Snowburst One is a stencil sheet with wide bridges between letters and tall lowercase, all of it built for attention. And Work Sans, a plain sans with thick-only strokes and tips that never creep together, makes the quieter partner.
gen-gf-tektur-manrope: Tektur arrives with pipe-cleaner strokes and outsized lowercase. It earns its keep big and short, while Manrope keeps a bright open gap at every curve and a minimal step from capital to lowercase.
gen-gf-unica-one-satoshi: Huge lowercase eyes with daylight inside every curve define Unica One, drawn at a single thickness. Satoshi, a plain sans with a soaring x-height, would crowd the heading if the heading were made small.
gen-gf-wallpoet-switzer: Switzer reads like tubular wire, with a tall waist line and sans tips that never creep together. Wallpoet earns its keep big and short, with paper showing through the line between its letters.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-fs-fira-sans: Tube-lit and loud. Tilt Neon has a splayed c terminal and a big x-height with short ascenders, while Fira Sans matches that tall lowercase with zero thick and thin contrast, so both feel built from the same pipe.
